Following yesterday's release of public beta versions of macOS 27, iPadOS 27, iOS 27, and other updates announced at WWDC26, Apple is now rolling out the first public beta firmware for AirPods Max 2, AirPods Pro 3, AirPods Pro 2, and AirPods (4th generation). Here are the details.

First public beta AirPods firmware now available

Last month at WWDC26, Apple announced several new AirPods features that will arrive alongside iOS 27 and other upcoming operating system updates.

These include customizable EQ sound controls to tailor the AirPods listening experience, as well as expanded GymKit support, allowing AirPods Pro 3 users to sync heart rate data through their iPhone.

Apple is also bringing firmware beta to AirPods Max 2 for the first time, which can be enrolled via a device running iOS 27 or macOS 27.

Following yesterday's release of the first public beta versions of iOS 27 and Apple's other upcoming operating systems, the company has now released the first public beta firmware updates for the following AirPods models:

  • AirPods Max 2
  • AirPods Pro 3
  • AirPods Pro 2
  • AirPods Pro 2 (USB-C)
  • AirPods (4th generation)
  • AirPods (4th generation, Active Noise Cancellation)

AirPods firmware version 9.0.314 has a build number of 9A5314b, which is the same as last week's developer beta.

Installing AirPods firmware beta

The following is Apple's official tutorial on enrolling eligible AirPods in the firmware beta program:

Enable beta updates — For Mac computers running macOS 27 beta or later: To enable AirPods beta, connect your AirPods to your Mac via Bluetooth settings. Go to "System Settings" > "Bluetooth," then select (i) next to your AirPods. In the AirPods settings menu, scroll down to find "AirPods Beta Updates." Use the toggle to enable beta software updates. — For iPhone and iPad running iOS 27 beta or later: To enable AirPods beta, connect your AirPods to your iOS device. Apple reminds users that after enabling the "AirPods Beta Updates" option, the firmware update will be installed automatically when the AirPods are placed in their charging case and kept near the paired iPhone or Mac.
